title: Multiplayer increment: is cross-platform support in scope or out?
summary: The Objective leaves cross-platform support genuinely undecided, and no agent may settle it by fiat. This increment's working scope is two players directly joining one real-time session (host/join by address on a local network) around the existing fixed-timestep simulation — but the success criterion does not say whether those two players must be on different platforms/OSes. Including cross-platform as a verified capability means adding platform build targets and a cross-OS acceptance matrix now: more cost and schedule, but the capability ships with the netcode instead of being retrofitted. Excluding it as a deliberate non-goal keeps the increment narrow and demonstrable, with cross-platform named as a later increment; the netcode can still be held platform-agnostic so that later work is additive. A middle path exists: bind the netcode to platform-agnostic transport as a hard constraint without a cross-platform acceptance test — most of the future-proofing at a fraction of the cost, but no verified cross-platform claim. Whichever you choose, the decision settles F-CROSSPLATFORM-SCOPE to DECIDED and fixes the scope edge the Definition currently leaves open.

options.label: Exclude — deliberate non-goal for this increment
options.description: Two players join the shared session on whatever platform this increment targets; cross-platform play is recorded as a named future increment. Scope stays narrow — no extra build targets or cross-OS test matrix — giving the fastest path to a demonstrated shared real-time session. The existing platform-agnostic transport preference is retained so the future increment is additive rather than a re-architecture.

options.label: Include — cross-platform join is an acceptance criterion
options.description: This increment must demonstrate two players on different platforms/OSes joining and playing the same real-time session. Adds platform build targets, cross-platform transport verification, and a widened acceptance matrix; higher cost and schedule, but the product capability ships now rather than being retrofitted later.

options.label: Include as a hard constraint, not a verified criterion
options.description: No cross-platform acceptance test this increment, but the netcode must be bound to platform-agnostic transport and input abstractions — promoting the current 'prefer not to couple to platform-specific APIs' hedge to a hard must-not-couple constraint. Cross-platform then becomes a later increment with no re-architecture. Buys most of the future-proofing at a fraction of the test-matrix cost, at the price of not shipping a verified cross-platform claim now.
